clue.text: Hospital excluded from surprise strike

indicators.note: excluded from tells us one piece is taken out of the other word

parts.note: a surprise is a shock
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital is left out of a sudden walkout by staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to hit or punch them, a colloquial synonym for strike.

clue.text: Floods area and struts around with no resistance initially

indicators.note: around signals the letters being moved about into a new order
with no means one letter is removed from the combined words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of resistance is the one taken

explanation.surface: Someone swaggers around an area that has been flooded, meeting no opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes the R that 'initially' takes from resistance before 'around' rearranges; 'struts' looks like a verb about swaggering but is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak or fill completely, so saturates means floods as a verb.

clue.text: Flower found next to ox-tongue?

parts.note: a wild flower whose name, split, describes what sits beside the tongue in a bovine mouth

explanation.surface: Asks which flower grows beside the plant called ox-tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Ox-tongue is also a plant name, so the surface seems botanical; really it is about a cow's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow spring wild flower of the primrose family.

clue.text: Intimidated by school admitting women

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school, taking boys and girls

explanation.surface: Someone is overawed by a school that has started taking girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cowed has been frightened into submission, a close synonym of intimidated.

clue.text: Angry counters from those on some bicycles

parts.note: cross means angry
bars are counters where drinks are served

explanation.surface: Irate objections come from riders on some bicycles.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbars are the horizontal top tubes on men's bicycle frames, found on some bicycles.

clue.text: Event that's cancelled with a loud cry

parts.note: a shout is a loud cry

explanation.surface: A fixture is called off amid loud protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is an event spoilt or called off, typically because of rain.

clue.text: Make runs — one hundred in classical style

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores a century in elegant classical fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, the plainest style of column.

clue.text: Information about mid-Welsh valley

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the information word goes round the other piece

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the five-letter word Welsh

explanation.surface: Someone gives facts concerning a valley in the middle of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, the usual word in Scotland and also used elsewhere in Britain.

clue.text: Producer of new art genre accepts Oscar

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the Oscar letter goes inside the rearranged letters
new tells us the letters of art genre are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film producer pioneering a new kind of art wins an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; 'Producer' suggests film, but it is a machine producing power.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator is something that produces, especially a machine producing electricity.

clue.text: Intense time being accommodated by former engineers

indicators.note: being accommodated by means housed within, so the time letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A tough spell billeted with former army engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means very intense or great in degree, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Doctor forgets net worth of such a stalwart

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician overlooks the net value of a reliable supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal working on FORGETS NET WORTH; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower of strength is an idiom for a person who is a dependable source of support, a stalwart.

clue.text: Answers without pressure from banks

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the pressure letter is dropped from the other word

parts.note: replies are answers
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Replies come in from banks once the pressure is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests riverbanks or lenders, but it is the verb, as in 'banks on'; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to rely on it, so banks and relies are synonyms in the sense of depends.

clue.text: Happened to see copper in record breakout!

indicators.note: in tells us the copper symbol is put inside the other word
a breakout is an escape that scatters things, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A news report announces that a police officer witnessed a record-breaking prison escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, and 'breakout' suggests a jailbreak while it signals the rearrangement of RECOCURD; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurred and happened are direct synonyms, both meaning took place.

clue.text: An actor might be the sort to mould

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
to cast is to mould metal or plaster into shape

explanation.surface: A theatrical remark that the actor's kind is easily shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor repeatedly given the same kind of role is described as typecast, so the phrase is completed by the adjective.

clue.text: My previous wife made demands and shouted!

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
claimed means demanded as a right

explanation.surface: A divorcee recalls an ex-wife who kept making demands and yelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclaimed means cried out suddenly, a synonym for shouted.

clue.text: Appreciate the referee showing restraint

indicators.note: showing means the answer is on display within the run of words Appreciate the referee

explanation.surface: Thank the official for displaying self-control on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appreciate' looks like a verb to define, but the answer sits across the end of Appreciate, all of 'the' and the start of referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain that restrains an animal, so it is a physical restraint.

clue.text: Changing role within board is bearable

indicators.note: within tells us the rearranged letters sit inside the board word

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: changing means the letters of role are altered in order

explanation.surface: Switching roles on the company board is just about acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' gives OLER from role, and 'within' places it inside the board word; 'board' suggests directors, but it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means able to be endured, a direct synonym of bearable.

clue.text: People with a cavalier outlook worry Syria lots

indicators.note: to worry is to harass or shake about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Carefree people are said to fret a great deal about Syria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavalier' looks like carefree, but Cavaliers were the supporters of King Charles I in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cavaliers were royalists, loyal to the crown, so royalist people share their outlook.

clue.text: What was in store for an old offender?

definitions.text: What was in store for an old offender?

parts.words: What was in store for an old offender?
parts.note: read as what lay ahead for a wrongdoer of old, the wooden frame for public punishment; read literally, the goods held in a shop's store

explanation.surface: A question about what fate awaited a criminal in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: The stocks were a wooden frame used to punish offenders, and stocks are also goods kept in store.

clue.text: Fifth columnist's gold chasing characteristic

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the gold letters come after the other piece

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A secret agent hunts for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth columnist is a secret sympathiser working against their own side, that is a betrayer.

clue.text: The speed of fame — not British

indicators.note: not tells us the British letter is to be absent from the other word

parts.note: celebrity is fame

explanation.surface: A remark that fame comes quickly, except perhaps in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is a formal word for swiftness or speed of movement.

clue.text: Tidy profit?

definitions.meaning: to tidy up, put a room in order
to make a big gain, as in a handsome killing on the markets

explanation.definitionFit: To clean up means both to tidy a place and to make a large profit.

clue.text: Little intelligence copper's got clearly defined

parts.note: info is short for information, intelligence cut down
Cu is the symbol for copper, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A slow-witted policeman has finally become sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link word; 'copper' is the metal here, not the police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in focus is sharp and clearly defined, as in a photograph.

clue.text: A bit taken aback with worthless store of information

indicators.note: taken aback is read literally as turned backwards, so the first pair of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
base means low or of little worth, as in base metals

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly startled by a worthless collection of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but reverses A TAD to give DATA; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is an organised store of information, usually held on a computer.

clue.text: Designate a charge for crossing back

indicators.note: back tells us the toll word is read in reverse

parts.note: a toll is a fee for crossing a bridge or road

explanation.surface: A fee set for making the return crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or designate something to a particular purpose or person.

clue.text: Regretting game point, starts to fear uncertain leader

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A team leader regrets a game point, beginning to fear the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means feeling or showing regret, so it substitutes for regretting as an adjective of state.

clue.text: Tripping in front of apartment buildings' barriers

indicators.note: in front of means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: tripping is stumbling
blocks of flats are apartment buildings

explanation.surface: Someone trips at the barriers outside tower blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbling blocks are obstacles or barriers to progress, figuratively speaking.

clue.text: Fresh air by day — and dry!

indicators.note: fresh means new or remade, so the letters of air are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather report: fresh air during the day, and no rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means very dry, especially of land or climate with little rain.

clue.text: A fencer's need to be on time for such accommodation

indicators.note: to be on means placed after, the sword following the time letter in an across answer

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword, something a fencer needs

explanation.surface: A fencer needs to be punctual to compete in such a setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'such accommodation' points back to the shape of the clue, tent-like lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent used as a dwelling by Plains peoples, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Requests fool to entertain king

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or take in, so the king letter goes inside the fool word

parts.note: an ass is a fool
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A jester is asked to amuse the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Asks and requests are synonyms as verbs in the third person.
